extra_exp_info: Delay exposure and double exposure in the section "Effects of fungicides on Bd growth on frogs in the laboratory"
note:
(1) Effects of fungicides on Bd growth on frogs in the laboratory: Extracted --> 4 fungicide treatments (Mancozeb, Azoxystrobin, Chlorothalonil, or no drug; reapplied weekly until metamorphosis) * 4 dfferent timings when the frogs were exposed to Bd (tadpole only; metamorph only; both tadpole and metamorph; no Bd). Do not consider "no Bd" or "tadpole Bd only" (= simultaneous exposure; because the timing of drug exposure and Bd exposure occurred simultaneously, so cannot separate causeÐeffect). Only consider the data with "metamorph Bd exposure" because the fungicide treatment ended at metamorphosis 
_ There are two groups: Bd exposure for metamorphs (=delayed exposure) & Bd exposure for both tadpole and metamorph (=double exposure)
_ We can test the effect of 'synthetic pesticide' using the data within "delayed exposure" group (i.e. no tadpole Bd exposure -> metamorph "with" versus "without" tadpole antifungal bath) => animals with one type of antifungal versus animals with sham bath
_ We can test the effect of 'live pathogen' by comparing data between Òdouble exposure: no fungicideÓ and Òdelayed exposure: no fungicideÓ. That is, in the absence of fungicide, comparing metamorphs with versus without tadpole-stage Bd exposure. Importantly, for animals in the Òdouble exposureÓ treatment, I only extracted data from those that were Bd-free at the beginning of their second exposure (i.e., uninfected at metamorphosis).
_ Note: I did not consider the comparison between Òtadpole fungicide exposure + tadpole Bd exposureÓ in double exposure versus Òtadpole fungicide exposure + no tadpole Bd exposure.Ó Ð i.e. in the presence of a fungicide, metamorphs "with" versus "without" tadpole-stage Bd exposure. Not to include such comparison is because it is unclear whether tadpole Bd exposure acts additively or interactively in the presence of fungicide. Thus, the comparison of with versus without tadpole Bd exposure in the presence of fungicide is not equivalent to studies that only compare with versus without prior Bd exposure in the absence of any fungicide. To more accurately capture the effect of live pathogen only in our meta-analysis, I conservatively extracted this effect only in the absence of any other fungicides.
(2) Effect of the fungicide itraconazole on Bd growth on frogs in the laboratory: Not extracted _ re-analysis of literature data.
(3) Effect of the fungicide on Bd prevalence in the field: Not extracted _ Study detected drug concentrations in the field and associated Bd infection status, but the timing of drug exposure and Bd exposure occurred simultaneously (cannot separate cause-effect).
(4) time_intervals = 71 days in the Result text
